clue.text: See alley cat skit around in state capital

indicators.note: around here means the letters of the phrase alley cat skit are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a comic sketch about a stray cat somewhere in a US state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here; 'around' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of ALLEY CAT SKIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Salt Lake City is the capital of the US state of Utah.

clue.text: Colonial type with dog crossing lake

indicators.note: the dog's name is pictured stretching across, so it goes round the other piece

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A colonist and his dog cross a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L inside SETTER, splitting it as SETT-L-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist who comes to live in a new territory is a settler, a fair synonym for a colonial type.

clue.text: Phone up around lunchtime maybe for something from the garden centre?

indicators.note: around means the turned word wraps the other piece
in a down clue up means the word for phone is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
one o'clock is a typical lunchtime, and one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone plans to ring the garden centre around lunchtime to order a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'around' puts I (one, for one o'clock) inside it after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lilac is a flowering shrub, the sort of plant sold at a garden centre, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Gun I found hidden in heather, being attentive

indicators.note: hidden in here means the gun and I are tucked inside the plant word

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a gun concealed in heather while staying alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden in' places ISTEN inside LING, between its L and ING; 'found' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Listening means paying attention to sounds, so it fits being attentive as a near synonym.

clue.text: Be aware of refusal being broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard on air, so the refusal word is taken by its sound

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone is conscious that a rejection is going out on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being broadcast' says the word for refusal, NO, is spoken, giving a word with the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To know something is to be aware of it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Church shut up in old Ireland or part of England

indicators.note: in tells you the hushing word sits inside the old name for Ireland

parts.note: Eire is the older Irish-language name used for Ireland
sh is the sound used to tell someone to shut up

explanation.surface: A church closed down in Ireland of old, or perhaps somewhere in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' looks like closing the church, but it is the hushing word; 'in' places it within the old name for Ireland. Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheshire is a county in north-west England, so it is one part of the country.

clue.text: What is symbolised in mathematics periods

definitions.meaning: the multiplication sign is read as a word meaning multiplied by
periods of history or spells of time

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what mathematical symbols stand for, set beside lesson periods.
explanation.definitionFit: The multiplication sign × is read as this word, and the plural noun also means eras or spells of time.

clue.text: Ray hitting something is such an event

definitions.meaning: in optics a ray striking a surface is called by this adjective

explanation.surface: A physics-textbook remark that a ray striking a surface counts as a particular kind of event.
explanation.definitionFit: In optics the ray falling on a surface has this name, and as a noun the word means an occurrence.

clue.text: The old man needs shelter, that's clear

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: Father requires a roof over his head, and that much is obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or evident, so something that's clear.

clue.text: Dodgy steeple held together by firm device pointing upward?

indicators.note: held together by means the reworked letters close around the firm's abbreviation
dodgy means unsound or rickety, so the letters of steeple are reshuffled

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A rickety church spire is kept standing by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' gives TELESPE from the spire's letters, and 'held together by' splits that around the firm, after its fifth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescope is an instrument often aimed skyward to view stars, so the question mark marks a playful description.

clue.text: Passion of some woman I adore

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lover describes the passion felt for a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks out the letters running from woMAN I Adore.
explanation.definitionFit: A mania is a wild enthusiasm or craze, so it works as a synonym for passion.

clue.text: Lucy's little case

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Lucy lost her pocket; her surname also names a small hinged case worn on a chain

explanation.surface: A girl called Lucy owns a small box.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucy Locket is the girl in the nursery rhyme who lost her pocket, so her surname is also the little case.
explanation.definitionFit: A locket is a small ornamental case for a picture or keepsake, and is the surname of nursery-rhyme Lucy.

clue.text: Censure is delivered in hurry after third-rate grade

indicators.note: after means the grade letter comes first, with the rest following it

parts.note: C is the third grade after A and B

indicators.note: delivered in means the little word is placed inside the hurry word

parts.note: haste means hurry

explanation.surface: A rushed reprimand is handed out after a poor C mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered in' makes HASTISE, and 'after' puts the grade letter in front; a C is the third grade, below A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise someone is to rebuke them severely, a verb synonym of censure.

clue.text: Retrieve good article that's been given external restriction

indicators.note: the good article is given an outside layer, so the restriction word wraps it

parts.note: a rein is a check or restriction, as in keeping a rein on spending
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Getting back a quality item that has had outside limits placed on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been given external restriction' means GA sits inside REIN, giving RE-GA-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to get it back, so it is a synonym for retrieve.

clue.text: Behave as faithful sweethearts, so get day fixed?

indicators.note: fixed here means put right or arranged, so the letters of so get day are reordered

explanation.surface: A couple are told to set a date to prove they are committed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' looks like setting a date, but it tells you to rearrange SO GET DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To go steady is the idiom for being in an exclusive romantic relationship with one partner.

clue.text: What is faced by uphill walker, treading awkwardly

definitions.text: What is faced by uphill walker

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests clumsy movement, signalling that the letters of treading are jumbled

explanation.surface: A hiker struggles clumsily up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges TREADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope or incline, which a walker going uphill has to tackle.

clue.text: Little daughter getting wobbly in town

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter, little meaning shortened
wobbly means unstable

explanation.surface: A small girl is getting unsteady on her feet somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dunstable is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, so town defines it by category.

clue.text: European city to descend into bottomless abyss on island

indicators.note: bottomless means the last letter of the abyss word is cut off

parts.note: hell is often called the abyss or bottomless pit
to sink is to descend

explanation.surface: A traveller goes down into a bottomless pit on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottomless' removes the final L from HELL, leaving HEL, which is followed by SINK and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Helsinki is the capital of Finland, so it is a European city by example.

clue.text: Row about to impede girl and wise man

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

indicators.note: to impede means to get in the way, so the about word lodges inside the others

parts.note: a sage is a wise man
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A quarrel threatens to come between a young woman and a learned man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' here rhymes with cow, a quarrel; 'to impede' lodges the about word just before the last letter of DISAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To row (rhyming with cow) means to quarrel, a verb synonym of disagree.

clue.text: Bird — big one seen in sky at night?

definitions.meaning: a small bird that bobs and dives in streams

definitions.text: big one seen in sky at night?
definitions.meaning: the star pattern also called the Plough

explanation.surface: A question about a large bird visible in the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipper is a stream-dwelling songbird, and the Big Dipper is the North American name for the Plough constellation.

clue.text: Idiot in school who betrays classmate?

indicators.note: in places the idiot word within the school abbreviation

parts.note: nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A schoolchild complains about a fool who tells tales on classmates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the fool inside the school abbreviation; the definition is a descriptive phrase for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tell-tale who informs on others is called by this informal noun, so it describes a pupil betraying a classmate.

clue.text: Poet leading international organisation — a big hit

indicators.note: leading means the poet comes in front of the organisation

parts.note: Homer is the ancient Greek epic poet
UN stands for the United Nations

explanation.surface: A poet heading a global body proves a huge success.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'leading' puts HOMER above UN.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a home run is a hit that lets the batter circle all bases, a big hit indeed.

clue.text: Our Upper House is not of course unrivalled

definitions.text: Our Upper House is not of course
definitions.meaning: the House of Lords is full of peers, so it is hardly without them

explanation.surface: A remark that Britain's House of Lords is plainly not without rival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Upper House is the House of Lords, whose members are peers, so read cryptically it is not lacking peers.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means having no equal, the same sense as unrivalled.

clue.text: Generous contribution from popular gents

indicators.note: contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Well-liked men give a lavish donation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contribution from' takes the letters running across popuLAR GEnts.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean liberal or open-handed, as in a large-hearted gift, so it matches generous.

clue.text: A Head of University positioned in neat courtyard

indicators.note: positioned in means the picked letter is set inside the neat word

parts.note: trim means neat and tidy

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A university head is installed in a tidy quadrangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' gives U, and 'positioned in' puts it into TRIM, all after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is an open central court in a building, so it is a kind of courtyard.

clue.text: Foreign characters given one endless job, receiving nothing

indicators.note: receiving means the pieces take the nothing letter inside them

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the job word is dropped

parts.note: a task is a job
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Foreigners are given a job that never ends and paid nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the job's last letter; 'receiving' sets the zero-shaped O between the one and the shortened job. The iota is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so these are characters foreign to English writing.

clue.text: Mostly green, a foreign capital

indicators.note: mostly means the colour word loses its final letter

parts.note: lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A green, overseas capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims LIME to LIM, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, a capital abroad from a British view.

clue.text: Leftie, the Parisian about to become a church figure

indicators.note: about means the pieces before it are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: red is slang for a left-winger
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A left-winger from Paris is on the verge of becoming a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses REDLE to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a senior lay official in churches such as the Presbyterian, a church figure.

clue.text: One in a hand-to-mouth situation in which eventual outcome is uncertain

definitions.meaning: someone who nervously chews their fingertips keeps hand at mouth

definitions.text: situation in which eventual outcome is uncertain
definitions.meaning: a tense contest whose result stays in doubt to the end

explanation.surface: Describing a poor person living hand to mouth amid uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand-to-mouth' usually means living in poverty, but here it pictures the nervous habit of chewing fingertips.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who chews their nails out of nerves has this name, and so does a tense finish whose result is in doubt.

clue.text: Scented aisle laid out in shop

indicators.note: laid out means arranged differently, so the letters of scented aisle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fragrant aisle has been set out in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid out' rearranges SCENTED AISLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.
